relevance_note: Retrospective cohort of 21 Qatari ATS patients homozygous for SLC2A10 c.243C>G, reported mostly as counts, but a few people are individuated in narrative sentences, e.g. 'twin daughters affected by ATS' and 'multiple balloon dilatations of pulmonary artery branch stenosis were performed in another patient'.
method_note: Built with a short Python script from my own reading; spans checked verbatim by script. The paper reports the 21 genetically confirmed patients almost entirely as prevalence counts (Results 3.3-3.14, Table 1); Table S1 (genotypes) is not in the text. Rows were created only for people the narrative individuates beyond a single count: the patient whose father was affected and that father; the patient (other family) whose mother was affected and that mother; the IVF twin daughters; the patient with bilateral diaphragmatic eventration, lung herniation into the neck and subglottic narrowing; and the two patients who had cardiovascular interventions. One-feature counts ('n = 1', 'in one patient each') were not turned into people. These seven unnamed people may overlap (e.g. a surgical patient could be one of the twins or the hernia patient); the paper gives no way to tell, so they are kept separate with no merge. The affected father and mother: the paper does not say whether they were genotyped or whether they are among the 21 (cohort ages 19 months to 13 years suggest not); no variant rows for them. The twins: the paragraph is about the cohort's family history, but the paper does not state explicitly that the twins are among the 21 genotyped patients, so no variant rows and no cohort-wide values (ethnicity, vital status, aortic tortuosity) were given to them. For the other five cohort patients, variant, zygosity (homozygous), ACMG codes, Qatari ethnicity, alive status and aortic tortuosity come from statements about the whole named cohort of 21 ('twenty-one patients exhibited a homozygous pathogenic variant', 'All the patients in the study belonged to Qatari ethnicity', 'There is no mortality ... in our cohort', 'Tortuosity of the aorta was present in 21/21 (100%) patients'). Zero counts in Table 1 (arterial dissections 0/21, other aneurysms 0/21) were not used to exclude anyone (v4 zero-count rule). Consanguinity (15/21) and other counts were not assigned. Contradiction: the Results call the variant a 'homozygous pathogenic variant' and in the next sentence 'likely pathogenic according to ACMG classification'; both recorded in the pathogenicity cell. The Data Availability Statement cites a ClinVar accession; not used.
